claim: Virtually all fishes rely on flows of water to transport food to the back of their pharynx.
source: Virtually all fishes rely on flows of water to transport food to the back of their pharynx.
evidence: This is a general statement about fish feeding mechanisms presented in the abstract without specific experimental data but drawing on established knowledge.

claim: External flows that draw food into the mouth are well described.
source: While external flows that draw food into the mouth are well described, how intraoral waterflows manage to deposit food at the esophagus entrance remains unknown.
evidence: This claim references existing literature and established knowledge about external flows during fish feeding.

claim: How intraoral waterflows manage to deposit food at the esophagus entrance remains unknown.
source: While external flows that draw food into the mouth are well described, how intraoral waterflows manage to deposit food at the esophagus entrance remains unknown.
evidence: This identifies a knowledge gap in the field, which is the motivation for the study.

claim: Posteriorly moving water must, at some point, curve laterally and/or ventrally to exit through the gill slits.
source: In theory, the posteriorly moving water must, at some point, curve laterally and/or ventrally to exit through the gill slits.
evidence: This is a theoretical inference based on the anatomy and physics of water flow in fish.

claim: Such flows would eventually carry food away from the esophagus instead of toward it.
source: Such flows would eventually carry food away from the esophagus instead of toward it.
evidence: This is a logical inference from the previous claim about water flow direction.

claim: This apparent paradox calls for a filtration mechanism to deviate food from the suction-feeding streamlines.
source: This apparent paradox calls for a filtration mechanism to deviate food from the suction-feeding streamlines.
evidence: This is a hypothesis inferred from the paradox described in the previous claims.

claim: The study developed and applied a new technique to quantify three-dimensional (3D) patterns of intraoral waterflows in vivo.
source: To study this gap in our fundamental understanding of how fishes feed, we developed and applied a new technique to quantify three-dimensional (3D) patterns of intraoral waterflows in vivo.
evidence: This describes the methodological contribution of the study.

claim: The technique combined stereoscopic high-speed X-ray videos to quantify skeletal motion (XROMM) with 3D X-ray particle tracking (XPT) of neutrally buoyant spheres of 1.4 mm in diameter.
source: We combined stereoscopic high-speed X-ray videos to quantify skeletal motion (XROMM) with 3D X-ray particle tracking (XPT) of neutrally buoyant spheres of 1.4 mm in diameter.
evidence: This describes the specific methods used in the study.

claim: For carp (Cyprinus carpio) and tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus), water tracers displayed higher curvatures than food tracers, indicating an inertia-driven filtration.
source: We show, for carp (Cyprinus carpio) and tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus), that water tracers displayed higher curvatures than food tracers, indicating an inertia-driven filtration.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data and analysis.

claim: Tilapia exhibited a 'central jet' flow pattern, which aids in quickly carrying food to the pharyngeal jaw region.
source: In addition, tilapia also exhibited a 'central jet' flow pattern, which aids in quickly carrying food to the pharyngeal jaw region.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental observations.

claim: When the food was trapped at the branchial basket, it was resuspended and carried more centrally by periodical bidirectional waterflows, synchronized with head-bone motions.
source: When the food was trapped at the branchial basket, it was resuspended and carried more centrally by periodical bidirectional waterflows, synchronized with head-bone motions.
evidence: This is a primary finding describing the mechanism of food repositioning.

claim: Aquatic organisms commonly exploit the dense and viscous properties of water to carry food from a distance, toward and through their mouth, by generating flows of water.
source: Aquatic organisms commonly exploit the dense and viscous properties of water to carry food from a distance, toward and through their mouth, by generating flows of water.
evidence: This is a general statement based on established knowledge in the field.

claim: These flows typically result from suction created by a powerful expansion of the feeding apparatus, for example, in fishes that suddenly increase the volume of their buccopharyngeal cavity.
source: These flows typically result from suction created by a powerful expansion of the feeding apparatus, for example, in fishes that suddenly increase the volume of their buccopharyngeal cavity (Alexander, 1969).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: A wide range of aquatic vertebrates across a large size range employ suction feeding: from larval fishes and frog tadpoles to whales, and some carnivorous plant with tiny suction traps.
source: A wide range of aquatic vertebrates across a large size range employ suction feeding: from larval fishes (Drost et al., 1988) and frog tadpoles (Deban and Olson, 2002) to whales (Werth, 2004), and some carnivorous plant with tiny suction traps (Müller et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: Suction feeding plays an important role in all major aquatic habitats and feeding niches throughout the water column.
source: Because of this impressive diversity in organisms making use of suction feeding, it plays an important role in all major aquatic habitats and feeding niches throughout the water column (Wainwright et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: In virtually all fishes, waterflows generated by suction are essential for transporting food inside the buccal cavity.
source: In virtually all fishes, waterflows generated by suction are essential for transporting food inside the buccal cavity (Labarbera, 1984; Potvin and Werth, 2017; Wainwright et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: During suction feeding, the three-dimensional (3D) waterflow patterns toward the fish's mouth have been particularly well studied.
source: During suction feeding, the three-dimensional (3D) waterflow patterns toward the fish's mouth have been particularly well studied (Day et al., 2007; Nauwelaerts et al., 2008; Skorczewski et al., 2012; van Leeuwen, 1984).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: Waterflow patterns external to the mouth depend on the approaching speed of the fish.
source: Although waterflow patterns external to the mouth depend on the approaching speed of the fish (Kane and Higham, 2014; Muller and Osse, 1984), instantaneous streamline patterns are fairly conserved between species and behaviors (Jacobs and Holzman, 2018)
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Instantaneous streamline patterns are fairly conserved between species and behaviors.
source: Although waterflow patterns external to the mouth depend on the approaching speed of the fish (Kane and Higham, 2014; Muller and Osse, 1984), instantaneous streamline patterns are fairly conserved between species and behaviors (Jacobs and Holzman, 2018)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: As the 3D streamlines converge toward the gape, food items that are initially somewhere close to the mouth will curve into the buccal cavity by these extraoral waterflows.
source: as the 3D streamlines converge toward the gape (Figure 1a, blue arrows), food items that are initially somewhere close to the mouth will curve into the buccal cavity by these extraoral waterflows.
evidence: This is supported by reference to Figure 1a and represents established knowledge.

claim: Food transport mechanisms inside the buccopharyngeal cavity are not as simple as external flow mechanisms.
source: In contrast to this relatively straightforward and well-resolved mechanism of food capture toward the mouth, food transport mechanisms inside the buccopharyngeal cavity are not as simple (Callan and Sanderson, 2003; Divi et al., 2018; Sanderson et al., 1991; van Meer et al., 2019) and are largely unknown (Day et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: Food transport mechanisms inside the buccopharyngeal cavity are largely unknown.
source: In contrast to this relatively straightforward and well-resolved mechanism of food capture toward the mouth, food transport mechanisms inside the buccopharyngeal cavity are not as simple (Callan and Sanderson, 2003; Divi et al., 2018; Sanderson et al., 1991; van Meer et al., 2019) and are largely unknown (Day et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work and identifies a knowledge gap.

claim: After passing through the mouth opening, water streamlines are generally assumed to diverge along with the widening buccopharynx.
source: After passing through the mouth opening (Figure 1a, blue arrows), water streamlines are generally assumed to diverge along with the widening buccopharynx (Figure 1a and b, red arrows; Muller et al., 1985; Provini and Van Wassenbergh, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work and reference to Figure 1.

claim: Inside the buccal cavity, waterflow tends to be directed toward the gill slits, located at the posteroventral and posterolateral head margins.
source: This implies that, inside the buccal cavity, waterflow tends to be directed toward the gill slits, located at the posteroventral and posterolateral head margins (Figure 1b).
evidence: This is an inference from the diverging flow hypothesis, supported by reference to Figure 1b.

claim: As flows take a short route to the gill slits, they seem far from optimal to carry food to the entrance of the esophagus, along the midsagittal plane of the buccal cavity.
source: Paradoxically, as these flows take a short route to the gill slits, they seem far from optimal to carry food to the entrance of the esophagus, along the midsagittal plane of the buccal cavity.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the inefficiency of the diverging flow pattern for food transport.

claim: There is no evidence that the esophagus expands in concert with buccopharyngeal suction generation to directly draw in a significant amount of water together with the food.
source: To date, there is no evidence that the esophagus expands in concert with buccopharyngeal suction generation to directly draw in a significant amount of water together with the food.
evidence: This is a statement about the absence of evidence in the literature.

claim: Other structures need to be involved in separating food from the waterflows.
source: Therefore, other structures need to be involved in separating food from the waterflows.
evidence: This is an inference from the previous claim about the esophagus not drawing water.

claim: The mobile pharyngeal jaws, while maintaining physical contact with the food, can move it to the esophagus.
source: The mobile pharyngeal jaws, while maintaining physical contact with the food, can move it to the esophagus (Liem, 1978; Sibbing et al., 1986).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Given the current hypothesis of diverging streamlines in the expanding buccopharyngeal cavity, food is more likely to end up being sieved by the other branchial arches and their gill rakers.
source: However, given the current hypothesis of diverging streamlines in the expanding buccopharyngeal cavity (Figure 1a and b), food is more likely to end up being sieved by the other branchial arches and their gill rakers, after which a second food transport cycle is needed, encountering the same problem regarding how the food is able to reach the esophagus.
evidence: This is an inference from the diverging flow hypothesis.

claim: Intraoral hydrodynamics are critical in determining the initial food deposit site after capture and, in turn, the associated anatomical adaptations and behaviors for food transport and handling inside the head.
source: Consequently, intraoral hydrodynamics are critical in determining the initial food deposit site after capture and, in turn, the associated anatomical adaptations and behaviors for food transport and handling inside the head.
evidence: This is an inference about the importance of intraoral hydrodynamics.

claim: Computational models of suction-feeding hydrodynamics show that flow can separate from the expanding buccopharynx to create a centralized jet of suction flow, along with anterior flow at the borders of the buccal cavity forming vortices.
source: Computational models of suction-feeding hydrodynamics (Thompson et al., 2018; Van Wassenbergh, 2015) show that flow can separate from the expanding buccopharynx to create a centralized jet of suction flow, along with anterior flow at the borders of the buccal cavity forming vortices (Figure 1c).
evidence: This is supported by citations to computational modeling studies.

claim: The central jet pattern could carry food closer to the pharyngeal jaws compared to the classical hypothesis of diverging flow.
source: This pattern, to which we will refer as a "central jet", could carry food closer to the pharyngeal jaws (Figure 1c) compared to the classical hypothesis of "diverging flow" (Figure 1b).
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on computational models.

claim: Gill arch and raker structures may cause crossflows, in which the main direction of flow medial to the branchial arches is directed toward the esophagus and only the permeate of the branchial filter basket flows out through the gill slits.
source: Thirdly, as hypothesized for fishes relying on filtration of smaller food particles from the water (Brooks et al., 2018; Sanderson et al., 2001), gill arch and raker structures may cause crossflows, in which the main direction of flow medial to the branchial arches is directed toward the esophagus and only the permeate of the branchial filter basket flows out through the gill slits (Figure 1d).
evidence: This is a hypothesis supported by citations to previous work on filter feeders.

claim: The spatiotemporal pattern of intraoral waterflow has still not been quantified in vivo due to the difficulty in gaining optical access to the buccopharyngeal cavity.
source: Despite this critical role during feeding in nearly all fishes, the spatiotemporal pattern of intraoral waterflow has still not been quantified in vivo due to the difficulty in gaining optical access to the buccopharyngeal cavity.
evidence: This identifies a methodological limitation in the field.

claim: This implies a fundamental gap in our knowledge regarding how more than half of all vertebrates feed.
source: This implies a fundamental gap in our knowledge regarding how more than half of all vertebrates feed.
evidence: This is an inference about the significance of the knowledge gap.

claim: The study developed a new technique based on biplanar high-speed X-ray videography to simultaneously quantify the 3D path lines of both food and intraoral water, as well as skeletal kinematics.
source: Here, we develop a new technique based on biplanar high-speed X-ray videography to simultaneously quantify the 3D path lines of both food and intraoral water, as well as skeletal kinematics.
evidence: This describes the methodological contribution of the study.

claim: The technique was applied to two distantly related omnivorous suction feeders, carp (Cyprinus carpio) and tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus).
source: We apply this technique to two distantly related omnivorous suction feeders, carp (Cyprinus carpio) and tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus).
evidence: This describes the study subjects.

claim: These species were chosen because their adult head size is small enough to fit the imaging volume of the biplanar X-ray setup, yet large enough to avoid hindrance from an intake of tracer particles for waterflow inside the buccal cavity using X-rays.
source: These species were chosen from the large diversity of suction feeders because their adult head size is small enough to fit the imaging volume of the biplanar X-ray setup, yet large enough to avoid hindrance from an intake of tracer particles for waterflow inside the buccal cavity using X-rays.
evidence: This explains the rationale for species selection.

claim: During each feeding sequence, the water tracers moved alternatingly backward and forward, interspersed with phases of stasis.
source: During each feeding sequence (carp: two individuals, seven trials; tilapia: two individuals, six trials), the water tracers moved alternatingly backward and forward, interspersed with phases of stasis (Figure 2, Figure 2—video 1, Figure 2—video 2).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental observations.

claim: At the beginning of the sequence, for both species, a relatively slow posterior motion of the water tracers toward the posterior part of the buccal cavity was observed.
source: At the beginning of the sequence, for both species, we observed a relatively slow posterior motion of the water tracers toward the posterior part of the buccal cavity (Figure 2).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental observations.

claim: The low velocity of water tracers at the beginning corresponds to the approaching speed of the fish.
source: As the velocity of the water tracers is calculated in reference to the entrance of the esophagus, this low velocity corresponds to the approaching speed of the fish.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the velocity data.

claim: The approaching speed was 3.9 ± 2.5 cm/s in carp and 3.3 ± 1.3 cm/s in tilapia.
source: It corresponds to 3.9 ± 2.5 cm/s in carp and 3.3 ± 1.3 cm/s in tilapia (Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This is quantitative data from the experiments.

claim: A rapid increase in the posterior velocity of the water tracers was observed, reaching up to 92.1 ± 59 cm/s for the carp and 97.8 ± 23 cm/s for the tilapia.
source: Then, we observed a rapid increase in the posterior velocity of the water tracers, reaching up to 92.1 ± 59 cm/s for the carp and 97.8 ± 23 cm/s for the tilapia.
evidence: This is quantitative data from the experiments.

claim: The rapid increase in velocity was named 'intake', corresponding to what is commonly known as the food-capture or food-intake phase.
source: We named this rapid increase "intake" (Figure 2), corresponding to what is commonly known as the food-capture or food-intake phase.
evidence: This is a definition of terminology used in the study.

claim: For the carp and tilapia, the intake phase lasted 0.26 ± 0.04 s and 0.27 ± 0.08 s, respectively.
source: For the carp and tilapia, this phase lasted 0.26 ± 0.04 s and 0.27 ± 0.08 s, respectively.
evidence: This is quantitative data from the experiments.

claim: After the intake, a phase of apparent stasis occurred, with a steady, low-velocity, anteroposterior water tracer trajectory, leading to a nearly complete stop of the food.
source: After the intake, a phase of apparent stasis occurred, with a steady, low-velocity, anteroposterior water tracer trajectory, leading to a nearly complete stop of the food.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental observations.

claim: The water tracers started to move again after stasis, corresponding to the beginning of the intraoral food-handling phase.
source: Then, the water tracers started to move again, corresponding to the beginning of the intraoral food-handling phase.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental observations.

claim: The intraoral food-handling phase was characterized by lower velocities compared to the capture phase (the maximum during food capture was 32.9 ± 11 cm/s in carp and 24.7 ± 12 cm/s in tilapia).
source: This phase was characterized by lower velocities compared to the capture phase (the maximum during food capture was 32.9 ± 11 cm/s in carp and 24.7 ± 12 cm/s in tilapia)
evidence: This is quantitative data from the experiments.

claim: The intraoral food-handling phase involved bidirectional motion: reverse flows (rfs), defined by negative anteroposterior velocities of the water tracers, and backflows (bfs), with a similar but slower pattern than the intake.
source: This phase was characterized by lower velocities compared to the capture phase (the maximum during food capture was 32.9 ± 11 cm/s in carp and 24.7 ± 12 cm/s in tilapia) and the occurrence of bidirectional motion: reverse flows (rfs), defined by negative anteroposterior velocities of the water tracers (highlighted in gray in Figure 2), and backflows (bfs), with a similar but slower pattern than the intake (highlighted in green in Figure 2).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental observations.

claim: The succession of the intake and the alternating rf and bf phases were consistent across trials and could be automatically detected in the studied trials.
source: The succession of the intake and the alternating rf and bf phases were consistent across trials and could be automatically detected in the studied trials (carp: two individuals, seven trials; tilapia: two individuals, six trials) (Figure 2—source code 2).
evidence: This is a finding about the consistency of the observed patterns.

claim: The periodicity of back-and-forth motions (rf and bf) was consistent throughout the sequence.
source: We found that the periodicity of back-and-forth motions (rf and bf) was consistent throughout the sequence.
evidence: This is a finding about the temporal pattern of the motions.

claim: For the carp, the transition between the rf and bf phases happened every 0.58 ± 0.12 s.
source: For the carp, the transition between the rf and bf phases happened every 0.58 ± 0.12 s
evidence: This is quantitative data from the experiments.

claim: For the tilapia, the transition between the rf and bf phases happened every 0.40 ± 0.05 s.
source: for the tilapia, it happened every 0.40 ± 0.05 s.
evidence: This is quantitative data from the experiments.

claim: Among the 73 trials recorded, no water tracers passed the esophagus.
source: Among the 73 trials recorded, no water tracers passed the esophagus
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental observations.

claim: The food was successfully ingested in most cases (5 and 6 failures or spit outs of 34 and 36 trials in carp and tilapia, respectively).
source: however, the food was successfully ingested in most cases (5 and 6 failures or spit outs of 34 and 36 trials in carp and tilapia, respectively).
evidence: This is quantitative data from the experiments.

claim: The total distance traveled by the food tracers during the pooled intake, the rf, and the bf phases was significantly lower than the distance covered by the water tracers.
source: Among these trials, the total distance traveled by the food tracers during the pooled intake, the rf, and the bf phases was significantly lower than the distance covered by the water tracers (Figure 2—figure supplement 1, Figure 2—figure supplement 1—source code 1), demonstrating a different path between the food and water tracers.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental data analysis.

claim: The different distances traveled by food and water tracers demonstrate a different path between the food and water tracers.
source: Among these trials, the total distance traveled by the food tracers during the pooled intake, the rf, and the bf phases was significantly lower than the distance covered by the water tracers (Figure 2—figure supplement 1, Figure 2—figure supplement 1—source code 1), demonstrating a different path between the food and water tracers.
evidence: This is an inference from the distance data.

claim: During the intake, the food item usually followed a trajectory that was more dorsal in comparison to the water tracer trajectory in both species.
source: During the intake, the food item usually followed a trajectory that was more dorsal in comparison to the water tracer trajectory in both species (Figure 3a, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental observations.

claim: The food trajectory remained close to the midsagittal plane, whereas the water tracers tended to spread throughout the entire buccal cavity.
source: In addition, the food trajectory remained close to the midsagittal plane, whereas the water tracers tended to spread throughout the entire buccal cavity (Figure 3a, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental observations.

claim: Among the dozens of water tracers captured by the fish during each trial, only 3–5 per trial also followed a midsagittal trajectory to reach a position close to the entrance of the esophagus.
source: Among the dozens of water tracers captured by the fish during each trial, only 3–5 per trial also followed a midsagittal trajectory to reach a position close to the entrance of the esophagus (Figure 3a, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is quantitative data from the experiments.

claim: The others spread to the lateral parts of the buccal cavity and stopped at the gill rakers.
source: The others spread to the lateral parts of the buccal cavity and stopped at the gill rakers (Figure 3a).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental observations.

claim: In tilapia, the water tracer deviation started more anteriorly.
source: In tilapia, the water tracer deviation started more anteriorly (Figure 3a, Figure 3—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental observations.

claim: In both species, the path curvature of the water tracers was significantly higher than that of the food tracers.
source: but in both species (carp: two individuals, seven trials; tilapia: two individuals, six trials), the path curvature of the water tracers was significantly higher than that of the food tracers (Figure 4)
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental data analysis.

claim: The higher path curvature of water tracers compared to food tracers demonstrates a more important lateral deviation of the water tracers compared to the food tracers.
source: but in both species (carp: two individuals, seven trials; tilapia: two individuals, six trials), the path curvature of the water tracers was significantly higher than that of the food tracers (Figure 4), demonstrating a more important lateral deviation of the water tracers compared to the food tracers.
evidence: This is an inference from the curvature data.

claim: Especially for tilapia, at the end of the intake, many flow tracers moved anteriorly after starting to curve in the lateral direction.
source: Especially for tilapia, at the end of the intake, many flow tracers moved anteriorly after starting to curve in the lateral direction (Figure 4b).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental observations.

claim: Anterior flow close to the borders of the buccal cavity is characteristic of the central jet pattern.
source: Such anterior flow, close to the borders of the buccal cavity, is characteristic of the central jet pattern (Figure 1c).
evidence: This is an interpretation linking the observed flow to the central jet hypothesis.

claim: In contrast to tilapia, in carp such flows occur only close to the mouth entrance.
source: In contrast to tilapia, in carp such flows occur only close to the mouth entrance (Figure 4a)
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental observations.

claim: Flow in the posterior half of the buccal cavity in carp resembles a diverging flow pattern.
source: while flow in the posterior half of the buccal cavity resembles a diverging flow pattern (Figure 1b).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the observed flow pattern.

claim: Posteriomedial flows in the branchial arch region, which would be indicative of crossflow, could not be discerned.
source: Posteriomedial flows in the branchial arch region, which would be indicative of crossflow (Figure 1d), could not be discerned.
evidence: This is a negative finding from the experimental observations.

claim: In carp, only a few of the many flow tracer paths were directed medially.
source: In carp, only a few of the many flow tracer paths were directed medially (see green tracers in Figure 4a).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental observations.

claim: In tilapia, none of the paths showed a clear medial component.
source: In tilapia, none of the paths showed a clear medial component (Figure 4b).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental observations.

claim: There was no correlation between the moment a tracer was ingested and its final location in the buccal cavity.
source: We found no correlation between the moment a tracer was ingested and its final location in the buccal cavity. For both species, the Kendall test of correlation between the location at the moment of ingestion (tz at the beginning of intake) and the final location of the particle (tz at the end of intake) was not significant (carp: p-value=0.27; tilapia: p-value=0.21).
evidence: This is a finding from statistical analysis of the data.

claim: Visually, it seems that early-sucked particles tend to stay in the medial plane of the buccal cavity, participating to the central jet, whereas the late ones tend to end up on the lateral parts of the buccal cavity.
source: However, visually, it seems that early-sucked particles tend to stay in the medial plane of the buccal cavity, participating to the central jet, whereas the late ones tend to end up on the lateral parts of the buccal cavity (Figure 4—figure supplement 1, Figure 4—figure supplement 1—source code 1).
evidence: This is a qualitative observation from the data.

claim: Generally, the particles tend to stay on the same side as their initial location, but there can be a change of side before the particles arrive close to the esophagus.
source: Generally, the particles tend to stay on the same side as their initial location, but there can be a change of side before the particles arrive close to the esophagus (Figure 4—figure supplement 2, Figure 4—figure supplement 2—source code 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental observations.

claim: A Kendall test of correlation revealed a significant correlation between the lateromedial location at the beginning of the intake phase (tz) and the lateromedial location at the end of the intake (tz) in carp but not in tilapia.
source: A Kendall test of correlation revealed a significant correlation between the lateromedial location at the beginning of the intake phase (tz) and the lateromedial location at the end of the intake (tz) in carp but not in tilapia (carp: p-value=0.000287; tilapia: p-value=0.07952).
evidence: This is a finding from statistical analysis of the data.

claim: The 3D kinematic analysis of the head bones revealed a stereotypical sequence of motions of the upper and lower jaws (gape), hyoid depression, and opercula abduction.
source: The 3D kinematic analysis of the head bones revealed a stereotypical sequence of motions of the upper and lower jaws (gape), hyoid depression, and opercula abduction (carp: two individuals, seven trials; tilapia: one individual, three trials).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the kinematic analysis.

claim: During the intake, a peak gape was followed by a peak in hyoid depression, followed by a peak in opercula abduction.
source: During the intake (highlighted in blue in Figure 5), a peak gape was followed by a peak in hyoid depression, followed by a peak in opercula abduction.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the kinematic analysis.

claim: This sequence of peaks occurred in each trial for both species.
source: This sequence of peaks occurred in each trial for both species (Figure 5—source code 1).
evidence: This is a finding about the consistency of the kinematic pattern.

claim: The abduction of the opercula is prominent at the time of lateral motion of the water tracers after they enter the buccal cavity.
source: The abduction of the opercula is prominent at the time of lateral motion of the water tracers after they enter the buccal cavity.
evidence: This is a finding linking skeletal motion to water flow.

claim: The kinematics during the bf phases corresponded to the same pattern of motions, but with lower magnitudes for the peak gape and hyoid depression than during the intake.
source: The kinematics during the bf phases corresponded to the same pattern of motions, but with lower magnitudes for the peak gape and hyoid depression than during the intake.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the kinematic analysis.

claim: During the rf phase, the sequence of peaks was inverted with respect to the intake: a peak in the opercula opening was followed by a peak in hyoid depression, followed by a peak gape.
source: During the rf phase (highlighted in gray in Figure 5), the sequence of peaks was inverted with respect to the intake: a peak in the opercula opening was followed by a peak in hyoid depression, followed by a peak gape.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the kinematic analysis.

claim: This reverse sequence of peaks, when compared with the intake, occurred in each trial for both species.
source: This reverse sequence of peaks, when compared with the intake, occurred in each trial for both species (Figure 5—source code 1).
evidence: This is a finding about the consistency of the kinematic pattern.

claim: The first application of neutrally buoyant X-ray particle tracking in biological research allowed quantification of 3D waterflow patterns inside the mouth of a live fish with satisfactory spatial and temporal resolution.
source: This first application of neutrally buoyant X-ray particle tracking in biological research allowed us to quantify 3D waterflow patterns inside the mouth of a live fish with satisfactory spatial and temporal resolution (time resolution: 750 fps; spatial resolution of the biplanar X-ray device: ± 0.1 mm; Sanctorum et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a claim about the methodological achievement of the study.

claim: Despite the inevitably low number of tracked particles (<20) compared to common, light-optical techniques using dense suspensions of considerably smaller seeding particles, the study managed to resolve the flow speeds and directions in the vicinity of the food.
source: Despite the inevitably low number of tracked particles (<20) compared to common, light-optical techniques using dense suspensions of considerably smaller seeding particles (e.g., particle-tracking velocimetry), we managed to resolve the flow speeds and directions in the vicinity of the food.
evidence: This is a claim about the capability of the method despite limitations.

claim: Compared to previously employed invasive techniques to quantify intraoral flows, such as endoscopy or pressure recordings, the noninvasive approach yields a more complete view of the spatial aspects of intraoral suction-feeding dynamics.
source: Compared to previously employed invasive techniques to quantify intraoral flows, such as endoscopy (Callan and Sanderson, 2003; Smith and Sanderson, 2008) or pressure recordings (e.g., Van Leeuwen and Muller, 1982), our noninvasive approach yields a more complete view of the spatial aspects of intraoral suction-feeding dynamics
evidence: This is a claim about the advantages of the method compared to previous techniques.

claim: The noninvasive approach allowed demonstration of the existence of different hydrodynamic mechanisms for food transport.

source: The new particle-tracking technique we described here (Figure 7a–d) can be easily combined with 3D motion reconstruction protocols for skeletal elements (i.e., X-ray reconstructions of the moving morphology [XROMM]; Brainerd et al., 2010) to link waterflow patterns to skeletal kinematics (Figure 5).

claim: The relatively straightforward, inexpensive, yet time-consuming protocol to construct the particles may be further optimized to reduce the variability in density.

claim: Optimized particles could be kept in suspension in the water column for longer periods and allow an accurate tracking for a wider range of waterflows, including those involving less strong pressure gradients than during suction feeding.

claim: Mold-based manufacturing protocols for metal-cored expanded polystyrene (EPS) spheres, currently available for relatively large particles with a diameter of 8 mm, could perhaps be miniaturized.

evidence: This is a speculation about future improvements to particle manufacturing.

claim: The method of X-ray particle tracking has strong potential to become an indispensable tool for studying form–function relationships and the biomechanics of various functions involving water motions to which we lack optical access.
source: In any case, the method of X-ray particle tracking has strong potential to become an indispensable tool for studying form–function relationships and the biomechanics of various functions involving water motions to which we lack optical access.
evidence: This is a speculation about the future impact of the method.

claim: The main question of the study was how food ends up at the esophagus entrance when the water that carries the food is traveling elsewhere – namely, to the outflow at the gill slits.
source: The main question of our study was how food ends up at the esophagus entrance when the water that carries the food is traveling elsewhere – namely, to the outflow at the gill slits.
evidence: This states the central research question of the study.

claim: If water was a pure 'carrier' of the food, it would follow the water tracer's trajectory from the entrance of the buccal cavity to end up in physical contact with the gill rakers.
source: If water was a pure "carrier" of the food, it would follow our water tracer's trajectory from the entrance of the buccal cavity to end up in physical contact with the gill rakers (Figure 1).
evidence: This is a hypothetical scenario used to frame the research question.

claim: Both carp and tilapia appeared to be well capable of positioning the food close to the midsagittal streamlines, thereby avoiding the food from becoming laterally deviated and ending up adhering to the branchial basket.
source: However, both carp and tilapia appeared to be well capable of positioning the food close to the midsagittal streamlines, thereby avoiding the food from becoming laterally deviated and ending up adhering to the branchial basket.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental observations.

claim: Despite the fact that only a small proportion of the water path lines passed close to the pharyngeal jaws, direct interception of the food item by the pharyngeal jaw was common, which avoided the need for subsequent intraoral food-handling actions.
source: Despite the fact that only a small proportion of the water path lines passed close to the pharyngeal jaws (Figure 3), direct interception of the food item by the pharyngeal jaw was common, which avoided the need for subsequent intraoral food-handling actions.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental observations.

claim: Fish make use of two mechanisms to cause the food to follow a midsagittal trajectory toward the esophagus: (1) developing a 'central jet' flow pattern inside the buccal cavity and (2) exploiting the food's inertia and finite size.
source: We hypothesize that fish make use of two mechanisms to cause the food to follow a midsagittal trajectory toward the esophagus: (1) developing a "central jet" flow pattern inside the buccal cavity (Figure 1c) and (2) exploiting the food's inertia and finite size.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the experimental findings.

claim: The study found support for the first mechanism by showing a centrally concentrated flow with reverse flow developing near the borders of the buccal cavity.
source: Our study found support for the first mechanism by showing a centrally concentrated flow with reverse flow developing near the borders of the buccal cavity (Figures 4 and 6, Figure 6—video 1).
evidence: This is a claim about the evidence supporting the central jet hypothesis.

claim: The central jet was previously reported in computational modeling studies, but was not given any attention thus far.
source: This central jet (Figure 1c) was previously reported in computational modeling studies (Thompson et al., 2018; Van Wassenbergh, 2015; Figure 6), but was not given any attention thus far.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the finding in relation to previous work.

claim: It was thought to be an artifact of not having included a water outflow trough gill slits in 3D models of expanding heads or a potential artifact of the hydrodynamic simplification in models using steady flow conditions in nonexpanding heads.
source: It was thought to be an artifact of not having included a water outflow trough gill slits in 3D models of expanding heads (Figure 6a; Thompson et al., 2018) or a potential artifact of the hydrodynamic simplification in models using steady flow conditions in nonexpanding heads (Figure 6b; Provini and Van Wassenbergh, 2018).
evidence: This is a claim about previous interpretations of the central jet in models.

claim: The current experimental results show that similar central jet patterns can be present in vivo.
source: However, the current experimental results show that similar central jet patterns can be present in vivo.
evidence: This is a primary finding that validates the computational models.

claim: The computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models indicate that a diverging flow pattern gradually transitions into a central jet by narrowing in course of the suction event.
source: The computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models indicate that a diverging flow pattern (Figure 1b; Figure 6a at 2.5 ms) gradually transitions into a central jet by narrowing in course of the suction event.
evidence: This is a finding from computational models.

claim: A narrowing of the main suction stream will increase the chance of food interception close to the esophagus entrance by the pharyngeal jaws, which will enhance suction efficiency.
source: Since a narrowing of the main suction stream will increase the chance of food interception close to the esophagus entrance by the pharyngeal jaws (Figure 1b and c), this will enhance suction efficiency.
evidence: This is an inference about the functional significance of the central jet.

claim: Further research will be required to unravel why the central jet was more prominent in tilapia compared to carp, which should be related to differences in mouth shape, buccal cavity shape, or expansion kinematics.
source: Further research will be required to unravel why the central jet was more prominent in tilapia (Figure 4b) compared to carp (Figure 4a), which should be related to differences in mouth shape, buccal cavity shape, or expansion kinematics.
evidence: This is a speculation about future research directions.

claim: The path curvature from a dorsoventral viewing perspective was significantly higher for the water tracers compared to the food tracers, indicating that inertial effects are at play.
source: Secondly, the path curvature from a dorsoventral viewing perspective was significantly higher for the water tracers compared to the food tracers (Figure 4), indicating that inertial effects are at play.
evidence: This is a primary finding and interpretation from the data.

claim: For the large prey that fill the bulk of the buccopharyngeal cavity, such inertial effects would be logical and intuitive.
source: For the large prey that fill the bulk of the buccopharyngeal cavity, such inertial effects would be logical and intuitive.
evidence: This is an inference based on physical principles.

claim: The data suggest that these mechanisms, in essence a type of filtration, are also present and effective for a relatively small pellet.
source: However, our data suggest that these mechanisms, in essence a type of filtration, are also present and effective for a relatively small pellet.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data.

claim: A similar mechanism is hypothesized to underlie the process of crossflow filtration in filter feeders in the flows that pass close to the branchial arches.
source: A similar mechanism is hypothesized to underlie the process of crossflow filtration in filter feeders in the flows that pass close to the branchial arches (Sanderson et al., 2016; Sanderson et al., 1991)
evidence: This is a comparison to a hypothesis from previous work.

claim: The study shows that such an inertial separation mechanism is present at the full scale of the buccopharyngeal cavity.
source: but here we show that such an inertial separation mechanism is present at the full scale of the buccopharyngeal cavity.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study.

claim: The effect of the size, shape, and density of food on its trajectory in a flow field remains to be further quantified to fully understand the constraints of the observed filtration mechanism during the initial phase of food intake.
source: The effect of the size, shape, and density of food on its trajectory in a flow field, as shown in our work (Figure 3, Figure 3—figure supplement 1), remains to be further quantified to fully understand the constraints of the observed filtration mechanism during the initial phase of food intake.
evidence: This is a statement about future research needs.

claim: Flow patterns matching those of a branchial crossflow could not be identified.
source: Although flow patterns matching those of a branchial crossflow could not be identified (Figure 1d)
evidence: This is a negative finding from the experimental observations.

claim: The fish may not have employed the branchial crossflow technique because the food type that was offered may not require it to be filtered in such a way.
source: the fish may not have employed this technique because the food type that was offered may not require it to be filtered in such a way.
evidence: This is a speculation about why crossflow was not observed.

claim: The feeding process is far from finished after the initial capture in the buccopharyngeal cavity, especially in omnivorous species that perform food sorting and processing.
source: As shown in previous work (Olsen et al., 2019; Sibbing, 1982; Sibbing et al., 1986; van Meer et al., 2019; Weller et al., 2020), the feeding process is far from finished after the initial capture in the buccopharyngeal cavity, especially in omnivorous species that perform food sorting and processing.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Regular and periodical back-and-forth motions of the water tracers after the intake moved the food back and forth inside the buccal cavity, with the food finally ending up near the entrance of the esophagus.
source: We observed regular and periodical back-and-forth motions of the water tracers after this intake, which moved the food back and forth inside the buccal cavity, with the food finally ending up near the entrance of the esophagus (Figure 2).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental observations.

claim: Reverse flows, directed toward the anterior part of the buccal cavity and previously referred as 'back-wash', were previously observed in carp and tilapia.
source: Rfs, directed toward the anterior part of the buccal cavity and previously referred as 'back-wash' (Sibbing et al., 1986), were previously observed in carp (Callan and Sanderson, 2003) and tilapia (Smith and Sanderson, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: In carp, anterior movement of the food has been observed using X-ray videos, after which a muscular structure packed with taste buds – the palatal organ – is hypothesized to locally bulge to clamp onto edible particles between the pharyngeal roof and floor, while small waste particles are flushed through the branchial slits.
source: In carp, anterior movement of the food has been observed using X-ray videos, after which a muscular structure packed with taste buds – the palatal organ – is hypothesized to locally bulge to clamp onto edible particles between the pharyngeal roof and floor, while small waste particles are flushed through the branchial slits (Sibbing, 1988; Sibbing et al., 1986).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The anteromedial direction of the flows observed during the rf phase seems ideal to bring food particles from both the gill rakers and from the pharyngeal region toward the palatal organ.
source: The anteromedial direction of the flows observed in this study during the rf phase (Figure 3b) seems ideal to bring food particles from both the gill rakers and from the pharyngeal region toward the palatal organ.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the functional significance of the observed flows.

claim: These back-and-forth flows are clearly important in the process of sorting food items from the nonedible particles present in the ingested water, and they potentially also prevent the gill slits from clogging.
source: Overall, these back-and-forth flows are clearly important in the process of sorting food items from the nonedible particles present in the ingested water, and they potentially also prevent the gill slits from clogging.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the functional significance of the back-and-forth flows.

claim: Reverse flows most likely involve the gill slit functioning as a flow inlet, a function that has rarely been studied.
source: Rfs most likely involve the gill slit functioning as a flow inlet, a function that has rarely been studied (Van Wassenbergh et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an inference supported by a citation.

claim: The data provide the first empirical evidence of bidirectional waterflows being synchronized with motions of the upper and lower jaws, hyoid, and opercula to create anterior-to-posterior waves during bfs and posterior-to-anterior waves during rfs.
source: Our data provide the first empirical evidence of bidirectional waterflows being synchronized with motions of the upper and lower jaws, hyoid, and opercula to create anterior-to-posterior waves during bfs and posterior-to-anterior waves during rfs.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study.

claim: The anterior-to-posterior wave of head expansion and compression is already well known in fish.
source: The anterior-to-posterior wave of head expansion and compression is already well known in fish (Gibb and Ferry-Graham, 2005; Lauder, 1985; Muller and Osse, 1984; Van Wassenbergh et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The anterior-to-posterior wave is interpreted as a mechanism to both ingest and dynamically accommodate a volume of water as it moves anteroposteriorly through the buccal cavity.
source: This is interpreted as a mechanism to both ingest and dynamically accommodate a volume of water as it moves anteroposteriorly through the buccal cavity.
evidence: This is an interpretation from previous work.

claim: For both species studied, this classical anterior-to-posterior wave was also observed during the consecutive periodic bf motions.
source: For both species studied, this classical anterior-to-posterior wave was also observed during the consecutive periodic bf motions.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental observations.

claim: The associated waterflow was not purely anterior-to-posteriorly directed: the water was also guided toward the ventral part of the buccal cavity by the hyoid depression, and it deviated toward the gill covers via the abduction of the opercula.
source: Yet, the associated waterflow was not purely anterior-to-posteriorly directed: the water was also guided toward the ventral part of the buccal cavity (Figure 3) by the hyoid depression, and it deviated toward the gill covers (Figure 4) via the abduction of the opercula (Figure 5).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental observations.

claim: During the backward motions of the water, no particles were observed entering the digestive tract, thus consolidating the hypothesis that no water enters inside the esophagus.
source: During the backward motions of the water, we never observed any particles entering the digestive tract, thus consolidating our hypothesis that no water enters inside the esophagus.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental observations.

claim: A wave in the opposite direction was synchronized with the rfs, as hypothesized earlier.
source: A wave in the opposite direction was synchronized with the rfs, as hypothesized earlier (Sibbing et al., 1986; Van Wassenbergh et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a finding that confirms a previous hypothesis.

claim: The stereotypical bf and rf alternations eventually lead the food to the centerline of the buccal cavity and closer to the pharyngeal jaws, where it will be actively transported toward the digestive tract.
source: The stereotypical bf and rf alternations eventually lead the food to the centerline of the buccal cavity and closer to the pharyngeal jaws, where it will be actively transported toward the digestive tract (Sibbing, 1982).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the functional outcome of the observed motions.

claim: The study highlights the biomechanical complexity of the processes occurring inside the mouth cavity during aquatic feeding in fishes.
source: In conclusion, our study highlights the biomechanical complexity of the processes occurring inside the mouth cavity during aquatic feeding in fishes.
evidence: This is a summary statement about the overall findings.

claim: The study showed how high-velocity suction flow patterns during the initial food intake phase can have an effect on the food's initial deposit site.
source: We showed how high-velocity suction flow patterns during the initial food intake phase can have an effect on the food's initial deposit site
evidence: This is a summary of a primary finding.

claim: Centralized suction streams may help to direct food toward the esophagus.
source: and how centralized suction streams may help to direct food toward the esophagus.
evidence: This is a summary of a primary finding.

source: The omnivorous species studied here during benthic feeding followed this phase by repeated, hydrodynamically driven repositionings as part of their food sorting and tasting abilities.
evidence: This is a summary of a primary finding.

claim: Future research using the X-ray particle-tracking technique could further reveal how these processes, and their intraoral hydrodynamic patterns, may vary between feeding modes, between animals with varying head morphology and size, etc.
source: Future research using our X-ray particle-tracking technique could further reveal how these processes, and their intraoral hydrodynamic patterns, may vary between feeding modes (e.g., ram-feeders ingesting larger volumes of water), between animals with varying head morphology and size, etc.

claim: Such studies would further advance our currently limited insight into the optically invisible processes of aquatic feeding in vertebrates.
source: Such studies would further advance our currently limited insight into the optically invisible processes of aquatic feeding in vertebrates.
evidence: This is a speculation about the impact of future research.

claim: Two carp (C. carpio) and two Nile tilapia (O. niloticus) were housed in two large water tanks at the University of Antwerp and provided with food ad libitum.
source: Two carp (C. carpio), carp 01 (mass = 341 g, total length = 25.94 cm) and carp 02 (mass = 304.5 g, total length = 20.42 cm), purchased from a pond shop (De Hof-Leverancier, Ekeren, Belgium), and two Nile tilapia (O. niloticus), tilapia 01 (mass = 488.4 g, total length = 29.4 cm) and tilapia 02 (mass = 489.0 g, total length = 30.3 cm), from a farm (Til-Aqua, Someren, The Netherlands), were housed in two large water tanks at the University of Antwerp and provided with food ad libitum.

claim: The number of experimental animals was reduced to a minimum for ethical considerations.
source: We reduced the number of experimental animals to a minimum for ethical considerations.
evidence: This explains the rationale for the sample size.

claim: As quantifying individual variability would require a higher number of individuals per species, it was not a goal of the study; therefore, intraspecific variation is not covered sufficiently by the analysis to allow generalizations within each species.
source: As quantifying individual variability would require a higher number of individuals per species, it was not a goal of our study; therefore, intraspecific variation is not covered sufficiently by our analysis to allow generalizations within each species.
evidence: This is a limitation of the study.

source: Additionally, the limited number of species studied does not allow us to generalize our findings to other adult, omnivorous, teleost fish.
evidence: This is a limitation of the study.

claim: The total number of individuals across both species (four individuals), the number of trials (carp: seven trials; tilapia: six trials), and the consistency of the results imply that the mainly qualitative conclusions on overall patterns in waterflow and skeletal motion are well supported.
source: Even if the number of analyzed individuals was limited to two per species, which may limit the interpretation of the data in the context of the STRANGE framework, the total number of individuals across both species (four individuals), the number of trials (carp: seven trials; tilapia: six trials), and the consistency of the results imply that the mainly qualitative conclusions on overall patterns in waterflow and skeletal motion are well supported.
evidence: This is a justification for the validity of the conclusions despite the small sample size.

claim: Prior to videography, the fish were anesthetized with 50 mg/L MS222 (ethyl 3-aminobenzoate methanesulfonate) and implanted with 0.35-mm-diameter beads made of a tin and silver alloy.
source: Prior to videography, the fish were anesthetized with 50 mg/L MS222 (ethyl 3-aminobenzoate methanesulfonate) and implanted with 0.35-mm-diameter beads made of a tin and silver alloy.
evidence: This describes the surgical procedure.

claim: Using hypodermic needles, four markers were implanted in the neurocranium, and three on the upper jaw, lower jaw, hyoid, and left operculum.
source: Using hypodermic needles, four markers were implanted in the neurocranium, and three on the upper jaw, lower jaw, hyoid, and left operculum (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the marker implantation procedure.

claim: The left suspensorium, left cleithrum, left fin, and two of the branchial arches were implanted with one or two markers for reference.
source: The left suspensorium, left cleithrum, left fin, and two of the branchial arches were implanted with one or two markers for reference.

claim: 4-mm-diameter food pellets were implanted with three 0.45-mm-diameter markers.
source: We also implanted 4-mm-diameter food pellets with three 0.45-mm-diameter markers.

source: After the surgery, the fish were kept under observation until full recovery.

source: The experiments were ethically approved by the University of Antwerp (ECD-2017-22).

claim: The water tracers had to fulfill two typically incompatible requirements: (1) being radio-opaque to be trackable on the X-ray videos and (2) being small enough and neutrally buoyant to passively follow the water trajectory as closely as possible.
source: The water tracers had to fulfill two typically incompatible requirements: (1) being radio-opaque to be trackable on the X-ray videos and (2) being small enough and neutrally buoyant to passively follow the water trajectory as closely as possible.

claim: An easy-to-execute and cost-efficient procedure was developed to make spherical waterflow tracers of minimal size to be used with biplanar high-speed X-ray video setups.
source: An easy-to-execute and cost-efficient procedure was developed to make spherical waterflow tracers of minimal size to be used with biplanar high-speed X-ray video setups.

claim: Like the existing tracer designs, the study surrounded a radio-opaque metal with a closed-cell foam.
source: Like the existing tracer designs (Drake et al., 2011; Seeger et al., 2001), we surrounded a radio-opaque metal with a closed-cell foam.

claim: The foam compensates for the inevitably high weight of the metal so that the overall density of the tracer particle approximates the density of water.
source: The foam compensates for the inevitably high weight of the metal so that the overall density of the tracer particle approximates the density of water.

source: EPS foam spheres with diameters between 1 and 2 mm were purchased (Rovul, Middelstum, The Netherlands) and sieved to retain only those with a diameter of 1.4 mm.

source: The mean (± SD) density of the produced particles from the test sample (N = 19) was 994 ± 33 kg/m3 (Figure 7d).

source: Since only negatively buoyant particles were presented at the bottom of the aquarium surrounding the food (Figure 7e), the mean particle density was 1031 ± 14 kg/m3, with a maximum of 1049 kg/m3 (N = 11).

source: Lag during flow acceleration and overshoot during deceleration for the slightly negatively buoyant particles were relatively small (Figure 8c) and therefore acceptable to describe general patterns of flow during suction feeding.

source: The four implanted fish were recorded during their feeding on a marked food item surrounded by about 15 radio-opaque water tracers.

source: They were filmed at a resolution of 2048 × 2048 pixels and at a speed of 750 frames per second using the 3-D DYnamic MOrphology using X-rays (3D2YMOX) set-up at the University of Antwerp (Sanctorum et al., 2019).

source: The system consists of two X-ray videography systems, each composed of a Photron FastCam Mini WX50-32GB camera (Photron USA, Inc, San Diego, CA) mounted on a Philips Imagica HC 38 cm image intensifier.
